widgets_values:
Duration: 15 seconds. A cinematic teaser for a bleak post-Soviet crime drama with subtle decaying cyberpunk. Winter in provincial Russia under a heavy overcast sky. Desaturated gray-green palette, coarse film grain, cold natural light, restrained performances and stark compositions. Futuristic technology is rusty, cheap and integrated into ordinary Soviet-era surroundings.

Music throughout: an original melancholic Russian folk-rock ballad—quiet male vocal humming without lyrics, acoustic guitar, distant bayan and mournful strings. Slow at first, growing into a powerful emotional crescendo. Synchronize every cut to the guitar rhythm.

[00:00–00:02.5] Ultra-wide view of a frozen river at dawn. Snow drifts across blue ice; factory smoke merges with the low clouds. A lone man in a black coat walks toward the distant city.

[00:02.5–00:04.5] Interior of an old commuter train. Silent passengers stare ahead beneath flickering fluorescent lights. Outside the window, a gigantic rusted industrial machine strides between snow-covered villages.

[00:04.5–00:06.5] Close-up: a young woman’s bare hand touches the frozen glass of a bus shelter. Behind the ice, a broken holographic advertisement weakly repeats: “ВСЁ БУДЕТ ХОРОШО”.

[00:06.5–00:08.5] An abandoned Orthodox church stands beneath tangled power cables. A surveillance drone circles its dark bell tower while a flock of black birds suddenly rises into the gray sky.

[00:08.5–00:11.0] Static medium shot beside the frozen river. An elderly man gives the lone traveler an old metal key and says quietly in Russian: “Если вернёшься — значит, зря уезжал.”

[00:11.0–00:13.0] Rapid trailer montage synchronized with the musical crescendo: boots running through dirty snow; a cybernetic hand loading one cartridge into an old pistol; headlights approaching through a blizzard; a woman turning toward the sound of a distant explosion.

[00:13.0–00:15.0] Epic wide shot. The traveler stands alone in the center of the frozen river as enormous red industrial lights awaken beneath the translucent ice. The music abruptly stops. A deep crack crosses the river toward his feet. Cut to black.

Audio beneath the music: winter wind, train wheels, electrical buzzing, distant church bell, ice cracking and natural Russian dialogue. No subtitles, no glossy neon, no exaggerated action.
